Like most (I assume), I decided to check the game out since I'm annoyed at supercell for ruining clash royale and since I got interested after seeing it in the creator's youtube video. I'd love to say the game's good, I enjoy the little conversations between characters, and the game play is solid (if you like clash royale's game play). I like the little customization options (card borders, profile banner and profile character), but they really aren't impactful. That being said though, it's got many, many issues. A pretty important thing to note is the strange split screen that turns a lot of people away after their first run or so. It's strange that there isn't an option to change this, but I personally got used to it after playing for around an hour. The leveling system is unbalanced (any level 10 can pretty much solo a tower, many even 3 star on its own), the relics are underwhelming, the cards have no descriptions (not too big of a deal, but it'd be nice), and there are plenty issues with the AI of the troops (sometimes troops just ignore enemies that they'd usually fight in favor of walking straight for the tower). Overall, unless you don't minding throwing the few dollars for the game, it's just not worth buying in the game's current state. I'd say wait for a couple updates and see if they make any big changes, then come back and see if you like it.

This is one of those situations where I wish I could rate a game "meh" instead of recommended or not recommended. I wouldnt say the game is BAD. I think the concept is really good and I was excited to play this when I first heard about it before it released. I've always thought clash royale was fun but never put a ton of time into it because of the pay2win aspect and also I prefer to play games on PC rather then mobile (and didnt feel like emulating constantly.) The problem is that in it's current state, its pretty rough. Definitely feels like it should be early access. I'll just bullet point the things I think this game needs. -Onboarding. Full stop. There is none. If you've never played Clash Royale before, tough luck, have fun trying to figure out what is going on. There's also no way to read about the cards in your deck. So you kinda just have to start placing them and learn what they do (or which Clash Royale troop they are the equivlent of) just through trial and error. Not a single mechanic is explained. Also some kind of sound effect or something for when the timer is getting low would be nice, as well as for when you enter into overtime. -Settings. Of all sorts. The most glaring being that I hate the "optimized for widescreen" thing. They take the board and chop it so that half is on the left of your screen and the other half is on the right, along with your cards. It's very odd and clunky to try and play. I understand that it allows everything to be bigger on a widescreen but I would MUCH prefer the option to just have everything be smaller but the regular vertical view. Playing emulated Clash Royale on a PC monitor has always been completely fine for me. Also just general settings like being able to uncap the fps, change resolution, ect. Also I dont know if its just a visual bug or what but constantly a health bar will completely empty but the troop/tower wont die for several more hits. Quite annoying. -Difficulty. This game is... very easy. I am FAR from a Clash Royale expert or even player, but I beat the game on my first run. The AI kinda just places troops down. They dont have a strategy or reactions to the player aside from just placing their troops on the same side as yours. As long as you dont also just spam random troops, and actually use your troops somewhat strategically, you will win all the battles. They also didnt feel like they got harder as they went on. It was just sorta the same until the final battle, which was also just more of the same but with a gimmick -Variety. The game is quite repetitive. The previously mentioned poor AI certainly doesnt help, but after a run or two you're not really gonna feel the need to come back. There are "relics" which are your typical roguelike items that add passive affects and bonus to your deck, but you really dont feel that they're there at all. Honestly you could tell me they were bugged and not working and I'd believe you. They dont affect your run or "build" at all. There are collectibles and an endless mode but I kinda just wish the main game itself was... well... fun. -Roguelike nature. To piggyback off what I said about the relics, you dont get to build your own deck in this game. There are prebuilt decks, only starting with one and having to unlock all the others by beating certain enemies a certain amount of times, but like... that really sucks. Its a roguelike. The whole point of roguelikes is the ability to create a build by knowing what items and cards synergize well together and taking advantage of that. If you're choosing my deck for me and by default having all cards work well together, then its not even really a roguelike. Its just a Clash Royale clone with randomized AI battles. You can technically swap out cards mid run with an NPC trader, but there arent synergies or interesting builds because most if not all of the cards are direct rips of Clash Royale troops, who arent designed for this type of game. So it basically just becomes grabbing whatever cards are most powerful to replace ones in your deck that arent as powerful. It's not very interesting or fun. Even though im within the playtime that allows me to refund the game, im not going to because I do genuinely want this game to be improved. I think conceptually it's really cool and I would love to come back to it in sometime and get the experience that I want it to be. I just hope that it gets there. Also the game is like half the price of a Big Mac so its hard to really feel "scammed." TLDR: Conceptually the game is really good and the artstyle is nice, but the AI opponents, content and gameplay itself is lacking. I'd wait to try it unless you're especially into Clash Royale or just want to try it for the sake of it.

After 100% completing the game on the same day that I bought it, I can't say that I would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a fun and/or challenging experience. First of all, the opponents are incredibly braindead, even the final boss can be easily defeated in like 10 seconds even on the hardest difficulty. Second, this game's cards don't do much to differentiate themselves from the ones from Clash Royale. Third, the relics, which are supposed to make the game more unique, are all terrible and have no meaningful impact on gameplay. Also the game is mostly just gooner bait.

[h1]Great concept, flawed execution[/h1] Like many others, I was drawn to this game from the developer's youtube video and I believe that a Clash Royale balanced around a single player experience can be great. The free demo was pretty unpolished and unbalanced, but that was within expectations of a game jam game developed by a single developer. Unfortunately, many of these issues are still in the released version. First, let's start with some positives. The artstyle is extremely charming and as a weeb, I love the anime girl-ified variant of the characters (party girl is my personal favorite). The variety of different races plays into the the fantasy aspect much better than what Clash Royale does (filled with boring humans and goblins). Some of the player friendly accessibility features that come with this game being single player (e.g. instant deployment) are great additions to the game. Aestheta does suffer from some UI and visual issues. While the vertical display option exists on PC, the font size on everything is significantly decreased and it makes it next to impossible to read any text in the game without squinting. For that reason alone, I stuck with the horizontal layout, but it's difficult to get used to and is very unpleasant to look at. It's also disappointing that there's a huge lack of information regarding how much impact levelling up a unit does and how much stats it has. Want to know if it's worth upgrading a unit at the star credit shop or after a victory? Too bad. Should you swap out your cards at the card trader? Just pray that the card is good after you've swapped it out and can't return to the shop afterwards. Even from the level select screen where you can see a card's stats, it's lacking vital information that Clash Royale provides (i.e. mobility, attack speed, whether it's a building/spell/troop). As someone who learned to play Clash Royale last year, I could make a educated guess on what a card does by figuring out which Clash Royale card it was imitating. However, I imagined that a complete newbie to Clash would have an extremely difficult time learning the 60+ cards in the game with total lack of information. Finally, I can talk about the two greatest flaws of this game: Difficulty and balancing. I wasn't expecting for Starcraft Pro level AI from a $5 indie game, but it is very disappointing when the AI plays like a 2000 trophy player that doesn't know what a card does. In my 2 hours of playtime, I've seen the AI cast a spell (Void) on nothing or a 1 hp cowboy, deploy a 7 cost unit in the other lane while their tower on the other side is getting demolished, deploy a bandit directly into the cluster of units I've built up in a counter push, and so many other dumb instances that I can't list them all. On all difficulties of the game, I did the exact same push of Cattle, Cowboy, and Sharpshooter (For the clash players, this is ice golem, hog rider, and musketeer). The AI has clearly never seen the level of skill I was portraying because this push always either took their tower and let me snowball into a 3 crown, or I would take half of their tower and dismantle their counterpush entirely. Even on the hardest difficulty, I just have to wait for the AI to play something super expensive in the back and then spam all my cards in the other lane and I'd usually end up three crowning them. The "final boss" is a joke who gets three crowned faster than any other AI. As for balancing, I didn't appreciate 90% of the interactions or stats that changed. Somehow, this game's version of the Pekka is somehow worse because skeletons + any ranged unit will fully counter it you getting a decent counter push. The dynamite (aka fireball) can't take down a tower with 16 hp, and even if I understand that the developer dislikes spell cycling, does it really have to have its tower damage nerfed that badly? Goblin gang will take an entire tower for 3 elixir if not responded to, while guards won't even take half a tower. Not even unit/interaction needs to perfectly replicate Clash Royale, but it hurts that it game is very unbalanced. There are maybe 2 or 3 impactful relics in the game, while the rest practically do nothing. In particular, the relic that make card upgrades level up a unit by 2 instead of 1 is extremely game breaking and essentially allows you to be 2x stronger than the enemy even on the hardest difficulty. There's a relic that is even a complete downgrade: Cannoneer tower has no noticeable DPS increase, it literally just fires twice as slow. The goal of each match is to get as many crown towers as possible, so any defensive relic that defends your crown towers is practically useless. Maybe if the AI had more threatening pushes, then these defensive relics would actually be worth picking. However, bartender (cannon) + skeletons seem to defend all pushes. As someone who's craving for more Clash Royale gameplay but can't play it due of underlevelled cards, I really want Aestheta to be a good game. However, I cannot recommend it in its current state because the winning strategy is extremely stale and the game offers little to no challenge. If you wanted to know what it's like playing against mid ladder players that don't know how to defend and only know how to deploy mid ladder cards in haphazardly fashion, then look no further. Alot of polish and gameplay balancing would be needed for anyone to recommend this game over Clash Royale.

On the surface the game is very fun and and has a lot of potential. However once you start playing it for a bit you'll realise that the game is not balanced well at all, making it very braindead to play. The AI you're fighting is very slow, usually does not attack and also sometimes just breaks and stops doing anything. It's also very easy to get overpowered due to the leveling system and the relics. Sadly this means I'll give it a negative review. However I could see the game turning around if it's balanced properly and also more polished, besides these issues the game definitely could be great.

Everything about this game just feels unfinished. It's like the groundwork was laid out but nothing was polished up. It certainly plays well enough but between the AI and the lack of information available to the player it just feels weird to play and I find myself enjoying it less and less the longer a run goes on. First and foremost right out the gate the game feels absurdly easy for what it is. Other people have mentioned it but sometimes the AI can just break and not set down units or they set down units very slowly and its a pretty easy thing to defend against. The most difficulty I found was when they would have units that would spawn more units (the holy order has quite a few of these) mostly just because it's a lot of health bars to manage when one breaks into three or one keeps spawning more, etc. Managed to beat the first run and didn't even realize the game had relics just cause my first run had literally no relic chests available. I wasn't even aware that there was a shop until my second run because the way the game is set up with the left and right side of the screens made with mobile in mind. The right screen just looks like a status screen while the left screen has the map to select the next encounter and I just never noticed there were buttons on the right screen along the bottom. Which brings me to my major issue of this game, the sheer lack of information available to the player. I never played clash royale so I assume this is what clash royale is like. With no reason to interact with the right hand side of the screen because its just your character and your cards like some status screen I found myself looking to the map on the left to just figure out the next fight. However, there's buttons on bottom of the right half of the screen that are small and unimposing and even if you hover over them they don't tell you what they are (settings, ticket shop, status, collection, and chests). If you're someone who likes to adjust settings as the very first thing you do in every game you're gonna find that you have to start a run first before gaining access to game settings. You gain star tickets from I believe level ups and you have a limit to how many you can hold and there's a shop you can access on the bottom of the right screen to buy relics and level ups, yet the game never tells you any of this. After each battle you earn 1 to 3 upgrade points to use on your cards to make them stronger, but the game will never tell you what the upgrades do even if you hover over your unit to check. The only thing you see is the levels of the cards you can select and you have to wait to check their new stats after you get back to the map screen. Champions are a pretty big part of the game, but the game wont tell you what they do, just pick one and hope its good. If it's not good, then oops... Oh well? This game feels like there's so much quality of life options that were just never considered at all. I'd like to hover over my cards mid game to see their stats and such while I'm waiting on energy generation, especially if I'm playing a new character and want to familiarize myself, but you can't do that. I'd like to see how units work when I'm trading cards cause I'm just shown a picture and in the shop you actually CAN get a description when you hover over cards in the shop, but a description doesn't really show you how they work. The more I play this game the more I'm finding this game lacking in the most basic concepts. Seeing how a card changes when you level it up, seeing how a card works on the field before you make a choice, a proper tutorial to tell you how these things work instead of "place units on the field for energy, good luck." For 3 bucks I can see myself coming back to it every so often if I want a quick 30 minute game but there's just so much about this game that leaves more to be desired. It needs more time in the pot because it just doesn't feel completely cooked yet.

The concept of this sort of card game/rogue-like has a lot of potential. Unfortunately I don't think this game accomplishes what this sort of genre combination could accomplish. In most rogue-like/card games you have a lot of flexibility of what kind of deck you'll end up with by the end of the run. This game does not have that, even if you visit every single trader you will never end up with a particularly different deck from where you started at. as a matter of fact. you will probably just miss out on valuable level ups so it won't matter. I hope this concept gets revisited but for now this is a proof of concept rather than a complete realized experience

This is a good game, I like the art, and it's a fun little loop, but it feels... I dunno, weirdly unfinished? I don't know if there's a story around it, if so please tell me, but it feels like there's stuff missing here, and I don't just mean unlocks. Like, there's a freaking A.M. knockoff you can fight with his own dialogue and units, but you can't actually play as them. Why? There's a system where you get chests to unlock banners and profiles, but there's only 5 of each, and not even enough to cover all the characters in the game. Why? There's a ton of REALLY COOL and funny dialogue between all the characters and factions the first time they meat each other, but there's no way to have it pop up again after the first time you see it. Why? There's like this... Currency, system? But you never have to interact with it to buy stuff since everything is done by trading, it's only used for rerolling, upgrading cards (kinda?) and unlocking new card borders I don't even know how to equip. Again and one last time, whhhhhy? Besides that I love the actual gameplay, I hear it's like Crash Royal but without the toxicity and, assuming, pay to win meta bs. Art is POGGERS. Units interact very well with each other. For 3 dollars you get a very nice little game it's just... Again, it feels like stuff is missing and I don't know why because it's not an early access, it's released, and it's been out for a year so... I dunno man, what's up? Again, good game just what's with all the missing/limited features?
